questions.text: Which three groups did the Holy Prophet's (PBUH) social reforms mainly uplift?
questions.explanation: His groundbreaking reforms uplifted women, orphans and slaves.

questions.text: In pre-Islamic Arabia, what cruel practice was done to some newborn girls?
questions.explanation: Women were deprived of basic rights and some newborn girls were buried alive.

questions.text: According to Qur'an 49:13, the noblest person in Allah's sight is the one who is:
questions.explanation: 'The noblest of you in Allah's sight is the one best in piety, righteousness and reverence.'

questions.text: Which right did Islam give women regarding property?
questions.explanation: The Qur'an (An-Nisa 4:7) gave women a share of inheritance.

questions.text: What did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) say was necessary for a valid marriage?
questions.explanation: Women could not be forced into marriage; her consent was a necessary condition.

questions.text: 'Seeking knowledge is obligatory upon every ___.'
questions.explanation: He encouraged both men and women to seek knowledge: it is obligatory upon every Muslim.

questions.text: The word 'emancipation' means:
options: the act of being freed from restrictions, especially slavery
questions.explanation: Emancipation is the act of being freed from restrictions, especially from slavery.

questions.text: A 'patriarchal' society is one where:
options: men hold primary power and dominate
questions.explanation: A patriarchal social system is one where men hold primary power.

questions.text: In 'My Beloved Pakistan', the poet compares the flag to:
questions.explanation: 'Your flag of green and star so white, shines like a beacon in the night.'

questions.text: Which part of Pakistan is described as having snowy peaks?
questions.explanation: 'From snowy peaks of mighty North, to deserts glowing in the South.'

questions.text: What is described as glowing in the South?
questions.explanation: The poem speaks of 'deserts glowing in the South'.

questions.text: What does the poet encourage young people to do for Pakistan?
questions.explanation: 'We'll work, we'll learn, we'll stand' — the poem inspires unity, learning and service.

questions.text: The main theme of 'My Beloved Pakistan' is:
options: patriotism and love for the country
questions.explanation: The poem celebrates the beauty and spirit of Pakistan and expresses deep love for the land.

questions.text: The word 'beacon' means:
options: a light serving as a signal
questions.explanation: A beacon is a light or visible object serving as a signal.

questions.text: The word 'soar' means:
options: fly or rise high in the air
questions.explanation: To soar is to fly or rise high in the air.

questions.text: Newly coined words like 'hashtag' and 'unfriend' are called:
questions.explanation: Neologisms are newly coined words, many born on the internet and social media.

questions.text: What does the abbreviation 'DM' stand for?
questions.explanation: 'DM' means direct message.

questions.text: A 'lingua franca' is:
options: a bridge language between speakers of different native languages
questions.explanation: English is a global lingua franca: a bridge language between speakers of different tongues.

questions.text: Mixing English with one's native language in online spaces is called:
questions.explanation: Mixing languages in conversation is called code-switching.

questions.text: 'Taglish' is a hybrid of English and:
questions.explanation: Taglish = Tagalog + English.

questions.text: Why have abbreviations like 'LOL' become popular?
options: Need for speed and efficiency in communication
questions.explanation: These terms were born out of the need for speed and efficiency.

questions.text: Digital globalisation has led to a more ___ approach to grammar in texting and tweeting.
questions.explanation: Texting and tweeting have created a more relaxed approach to sentence structure and punctuation.

questions.text: 'Climate action' refers to efforts to:
options: reduce greenhouse gas emissions and protect the environment
questions.explanation: Climate action means efforts to reduce greenhouse gases, adapt and protect the environment.

questions.text: Burning fossil fuels for energy releases which gas?
questions.explanation: The burning of fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide.

questions.text: The rise in Earth's average temperature caused by greenhouse gases trapping heat is called:
questions.explanation: Greenhouse gases trap heat, raising the average temperature: global warming.

questions.text: Since when have human activities especially disrupted the balance of gases?
questions.explanation: Especially since the Industrial Revolution, human activities have disrupted this balance.

questions.text: In which year was the Paris Agreement signed?
questions.explanation: The most notable agreement, the Paris Agreement, was signed in 2015.

questions.text: Under the Paris Agreement, countries try to keep warming below:
questions.explanation: They committed to limit warming well below 2 C, aiming for below 1.5 C.

questions.text: Who is disproportionately affected by climate change?
questions.explanation: Climate change hits poor and developing countries hardest, though they contribute least.

questions.text: Melting glaciers lead to:
questions.explanation: Glaciers melting at alarming rates lead to rising sea levels.

questions.text: Who wrote 'The Happy Prince'?
questions.explanation: 'The Happy Prince' is by Oscar Wilde.

questions.text: What were the Happy Prince's eyes made of?
questions.explanation: For eyes he had two bright sapphires.

questions.text: What glowed on the Happy Prince's sword-hilt?
questions.explanation: A large red ruby glowed on his sword-hilt.

questions.text: Where had the Swallow's friends gone?
questions.explanation: His friends had gone away to Egypt six weeks before.

questions.text: Why did drops of water fall on the Swallow though there were no clouds?
questions.explanation: The eyes of the Happy Prince were filled with tears.

questions.text: In which palace did the Prince live when he was alive, where sorrow was not allowed?
questions.explanation: He lived in the Palace of Sans-Souci, where sorrow was not allowed to enter.

questions.text: What did the Happy Prince give to the poor seamstress?
questions.explanation: The Swallow gently picked out the great ruby and took it to the seamstress.

questions.text: Why was the little match-girl crying?
options: Her matches fell in the gutter and were spoiled
questions.explanation: Her matches fell in the gutter and her father would beat her.

questions.text: What did not melt in the furnace?
questions.explanation: The workmen said the broken lead heart would not melt in the furnace.

questions.text: Where were the lead heart and the dead Swallow thrown?
questions.explanation: The lead heart was thrown on the dust-heap where the dead Swallow was also lying.

questions.text: 'Drug abuse' means:
options: the harmful or wrong use of drugs
taking medicine on a doctor's advice
questions.explanation: Drug abuse is the harmful or wrong use of drugs that damages health, behaviour and life.

questions.text: Which of these is mentioned as a reason people start using drugs?
questions.explanation: People try drugs out of curiosity or due to peer pressure.

questions.text: Which organisation in Pakistan works to stop drug smuggling?
questions.explanation: The Anti-Narcotics Force (ANF) works to stop the smuggling of illegal drugs.

questions.text: Which group is especially at risk of drug abuse, according to the lesson?
questions.explanation: Many drug users are young people; teenagers and students are especially at risk.

questions.text: How does drug abuse affect society?
options: It leads to crimes, accidents and violence
questions.explanation: Drug abuse leads to crimes, accidents and violence, creating fear and insecurity.

questions.text: Taking sleeping pills or painkillers without a doctor's advice is:
questions.explanation: The lesson includes pills and painkillers taken without a doctor's advice as drug abuse.

questions.text: Which body parts can drugs damage, according to the lesson?
questions.explanation: Drugs can damage the brain, heart, lungs, liver and other parts of the body.

questions.text: 'Pollution' refers to:
options: the presence of harmful substances in our environment
questions.explanation: Pollution is the presence of harmful substances that damage air, water and land.

questions.text: How do trees help reduce pollution?
options: They absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen
questions.explanation: Trees absorb carbon dioxide, release oxygen, trap dust and reduce heat.

questions.text: Which of these pollutes rivers, according to the lesson?
options: Plastics and chemicals dumped in rivers
questions.explanation: Plastics and chemicals dumped in rivers pollute the water.

questions.text: What has contributed to the rise in pollution in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Rapid urbanisation and industrial growth have contributed to the rise in pollution.

questions.text: Many factories add to pollution because they do not follow proper:
questions.explanation: Many factories do not follow proper waste management rules.

questions.text: According to the lesson, parks and green belts in cities serve as:
options: peaceful places to relax and exercise
questions.explanation: They beautify the surroundings and serve as peaceful places to relax and exercise.

questions.text: Who wrote 'The Road Not Taken'?
questions.explanation: 'The Road Not Taken' is by Robert Frost.

questions.text: Where did the two roads diverge?
questions.explanation: 'Two roads diverged in a yellow wood.'

questions.text: Why did the speaker choose the second road?
options: It was grassy and wanted wear
questions.explanation: He took the other, 'because it was grassy and wanted wear'.

questions.text: Which road did the speaker finally take?
questions.explanation: 'I took the one less traveled by, and that has made all the difference.'

questions.text: The central theme of the poem is:
options: choices and their consequences in life
questions.explanation: The poem explores how choices shape our futures in ways we may not understand at the time.

questions.text: 'I doubted if I should ever come back' means the speaker:
options: felt he might never return to try the other road
questions.explanation: Knowing 'how way leads on to way', he felt he might never come back to try the first road.

questions.text: The word 'diverged' means:
questions.explanation: Diverged means split or branched off.

questions.text: Who wrote 'The Three Questions'?
questions.explanation: 'The Three Questions' is by Leo Tolstoy.

questions.text: What did the king promise to anyone who answered his questions?
questions.explanation: He proclaimed that he would give a great reward to anyone who taught him the answers.

questions.text: Why did the king give the reward to none of the learned men?
questions.explanation: All the answers being different, the king did not agree with any and gave the reward to none.

questions.text: Whom did the king finally consult?
options: A hermit renowned for his wisdom
questions.explanation: He decided to consult a hermit widely renowned for his wisdom.

questions.text: Why did the king put on simple clothes to visit the hermit?
options: The hermit received none but common folk
He was hiding from enemies only
questions.explanation: The hermit received none but common folk, so the king dressed simply.

questions.text: What was the hermit doing when the king arrived?
options: Digging the ground in front of his hut
questions.explanation: When the king approached, the hermit was digging the ground in front of his hut.

questions.text: According to the hermit, the most important time is:
questions.explanation: Now is the most important time because it is the only time when we have any power.

questions.text: According to the hermit, the most necessary person is:
options: the one with whom you are
questions.explanation: The most necessary person is the one with whom you are.

questions.text: According to the hermit, the most important affair is:
options: to do good to the person you are with
questions.explanation: The most important affair is to do him good, for that alone man was sent into this life.
